layers.note: A low rounded shrub of rocky slopes; at the bajada's 750 m, near its lower limit, only on rocky outcrops.

heat_load.note: Cool and sunny aspects alike; at its lower limit, cooler north slopes.

elevation_m.note: About 900 to 1,830 m (Kearney and Peebles: 3,000 to 6,000 feet); the full range is let down to 700 m so the bajada's rocky hills hold it.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 1 to 12 °C; gone below −2 °C and above 15 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −17 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −22 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 23 to 32 °C; gone below 20 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,000 to 8,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,000.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,500 to 6,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,800.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.1, gone by 0.05.

summer_rain.note: Needs the summer monsoon: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation falling in the July to September storms, gone below 0.15, where winter rain falls alone; the bajada gets about half its rain then. Up to about 0.8, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m) from general knowledge of the species, the ranges and elevations in Kearney and Peebles (1942) and, where one exists, the FEIS species review. Turpentine bush grows from western Texas through New Mexico and Arizona to southern Nevada, Utah and California and northern Mexico, mostly in desert grassland, chaparral and upper desert scrub above the Sonoran Desert proper (Kearney and Peebles 1942; Abrams and Ferris 1960). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
